name: Fibonacci (Dynamic Programming)
description: Computes the nth Fibonacci number using dynamic programming — either top-down memoization or bottom-up tabulation. Reduces exponential naive recursion to linear time.
aim: Compute fib(n) efficiently by storing previously computed values (memoization) or building up from base cases (tabulation), eliminating redundant recursive calls.
howItWorks: For each i from 2 to n: dp[i]=dp[i-1]+dp[i-2]
Each value computed exactly once (vs 2^n in naive recursion)
Space optimization: only need last two values

time.averageCase: Linear time — each value computed once
time.worstCase: Iterative DP: O(n). Naive recursive (not shown) would be O(2^n).

complexity.spaceDescription: DP array of size n+1; can be optimized to O(1) with two variables

realWorld: Number of ways to climb stairs (same recurrence)
alternatives: Binet's formula — O(1) but floating-point precision issues
Naive recursion — O(2^n), never use for n>30
